businessType: Third-party logistics provider serving retail, CPG, and e-commerce customers. 28 warehouses across Southeast US, 400 employees, $92M annual revenue. EBITDA margin 12% ($11M), down from 14% (three years ago). Profit pressure from e-commerce customer growth (higher operational complexity, lower margins vs. traditional retail) and rising labor costs.
stage: Mature profitable: EBITDA $11M (12% margin), operating cash flow strong $9M, return on assets 6.3% (below peer median 8%). Customer concentration risk: top 3 customers = 28% of revenue. Margin compression driven by (1) shift to e-commerce customers (lower margins), (2) labor inflation (+12% in 24 months), (3) automation capex requirements.
ownerGoal: Return EBITDA to 15%+ margin within 24 months through operational efficiency and customer mix optimization.
ownerConstraints: Labor market: Warehouse staffing tight; wages +12% in 24 months. Automation capex required to reduce labor dependency, but ROI uncertain.

Customer mix shift: E-commerce customers (38% of revenue) require higher service complexity (faster fulfillment, returns handling) at lower margins (8-10% vs. retail 15-18%). Traditional retail shrinking.
Automation capex: Modern 3PL requires significant capex (robotics, WMS upgrades). Estimated $8-12M to upgrade 28 warehouses. Current cash flow cannot support full modernization.
Competitive dynamics: Amazon Logistics, national 3PLs entering regional markets, competing on price and technology. Regional 3PLs consolidating. Scale matters for profitability.
Economic sensitivity: Retail/e-commerce volume sensitive to economic cycles; FY2025 e-commerce growth 8% (vs. 15% historical average).
immediateConcern: EBITDA margin eroding (14% → 12% in 3 years) while revenue growing slowly (5% YoY current vs. 12% three years ago). Growth slowing and margins compressing = profitability squeeze. Net income declining despite revenue growth. Must determine whether problem is structural (customer mix shift to lower-margin e-commerce) or operational (labor cost inflation, underutilized capacity).
